incidents.victim: Huntress, LastPass, HackerOne, Recorded Future, Jamf, Snyk, Tanium and other tech/security firms
incidents.vector: Attackers breached sales-intelligence vendor Klue and abused its OAuth tokens to pull connected customers' Salesforce (and some Gong) data, then extorted victims via a leak site.
incidents.impact: A widening wave of Salesforce data thefts hit at least a dozen technology and security companies; the Icarus group began publishing stolen CRM data and warned more victims would follow, raising follow-on social-engineering risk.

incidents.victim: Tata Electronics
incidents.vector: Data-theft extortion group World Leaks (rebranded from Hunters International) claimed it stole and published confidential files from the Indian contract manufacturer.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a cybersecurity incident; leaked samples allegedly include Apple supplier specifications and Tesla manufacturing documents, though the company said operations were unaffected.

incidents.victim: Transport for London (and US healthcare providers SSM Health, Sutter Health)
incidents.vector: Members of the predominantly English-speaking Scattered Spider group infiltrated TfL's network in 2024 using social engineering and credential theft.
incidents.impact: Two members (Thalha Jubair, 20, and Owen Flowers, 18) pleaded guilty in the UK; the 2024 attack forced all 28,000 TfL staff to reset passwords in person, exposed Oyster customer data, and cost about £29M ($38M).

incidents.victim: Customers of US banks (American Express, Bank of America, Chase, PayPal, Wells Fargo, Cash App)
incidents.vector: Algerian national 'SPOX' (Abdellah Belmili) built and sold ~595 phishing kits replicating major US bank login pages and ran two black-market sites (market0day.com, spoxy.us) selling stolen credentials.
incidents.impact: DOJ charged Belmili after extradition from Spain; the operation defrauded roughly 5,600 victims and moved about $900,000 in Bitcoin over three years. He also built backdoors into kits to keep harvesting buyers' victim data.

incidents.victim: Undisclosed organization (hybrid on-prem/cloud)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (plus second parallel actor)
incidents.vector: Storm-2603 exploited on-prem SharePoint vulnerabilities, then used legitimate tools (Velociraptor, Cloudflare tunneling, Zoho Assist) for persistence; a second unrelated actor operated in parallel using DLL sideloading and custom backdoors.
incidents.impact: Microsoft DART found two unrelated threat actors operating simultaneously in one intrusion, blending ransomware activity with quieter long-term access and complicating attribution before the intrusion was contained.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate firewall operators worldwide (incl. a NATO-aligned defense contractor)
incidents.vector: Russian-speaking actors brute-forced and credential-stuffed internet-exposed FortiGate admin/VPN interfaces, then deployed a Golang 'FortigateSniffer' tool abusing FortiOS diagnostic commands to passively capture authentication traffic across 24 protocols.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' campaign exposed valid credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate URLs across 194 countries and harvested 110M+ credentials; affected sectors include government, telecom, finance and healthcare, with a Turkish NATO contractor's classified documents allegedly stolen.

incidents.victim: SocGholish malware infrastructure (Evil Corp / TA569)
incidents.vector: International law enforcement (Operation Endgame) seized servers and domains underpinning SocGholish, a JavaScript framework that uses fake browser updates and traffic-distribution systems to broker access for ransomware.
incidents.impact: Authorities seized 106 servers, remediated ~14,971 compromised (mostly WordPress) sites and recovered 1.4M leaked WordPress credentials, disrupting a key initial-access supplier used by the Russian Evil Corp gang.

incidents.victim: npm 'mastra' / '@mastra' package ecosystem (developers and CI/CD pipelines)
incidents.vector: Sapphire Sleet took over the 'ehindero' npm maintainer account and poisoned 140+ Mastra packages with a malicious 'easy-day-js' typosquat whose postinstall hook dropped a staged loader, disabled TLS checks, and fetched a tasking implant.
incidents.impact: Any workstation or pipeline that ran npm install/update during the window was exposed; the implant enabled arbitrary follow-on code, PowerShell backdoors, Defender exclusions and SYSTEM-level persistence before npm removed the packages.

incidents.victim: Silver Fox cybercrime group (victims largely in China)
incidents.vector: Chinese police arrested members who used malspam and fake download sites to spread the Silver Fox/Winos trojan, which then deployed infostealers and the AtlasRAT/ValleyRAT remote-access tools.
incidents.impact: 67 suspects were arrested across five provinces, including the trojan's author, in a crackdown on China's largest domestically focused cybercrime operation.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research institutions
incidents.vector: UNC6508 exploited externally facing REDCap research servers, deployed custom 'INFINITERED' malware to harvest credentials, then pivoted internally and abused Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive email.
incidents.impact: The China-nexus actor remained undetected for over a year (since Sept 2023), targeting AI, cyber, medical, uncrewed-systems and national-defense research before Google disrupted the infrastructure and notified victims.

incidents.victim: Bank Melli, Bank Tejarat, Bank Saderat and Export Development Bank of Iran
incidents.vector: An attack reportedly targeting shared communications infrastructure took down online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks.
incidents.impact: Online and mobile banking for the four institutions was disrupted over a weekend; Iran's banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.victim: Novo Nordisk
incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to parts of the internal network of the Danish pharmaceutical giant.
incidents.impact: Novo Nordisk took systems offline to evict the intruders and said some sensitive data, including patient PII, was copied.

incidents.victim: Humanity Protocol
incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly compromised a developer laptop and stole private multisig keys.
incidents.impact: About $36 million in crypto-assets was stolen and the Humanity token lost nearly 90% of its value shortly after the hack.

incidents.victim: Arch Linux users (AUR package repository)
incidents.vector: Attackers abused the AUR 'adopt' mechanism to take over abandoned ('orphaned') community packages and inserted install steps that pulled a malicious npm package (later swapped for a Bun script) delivering a rootkit and infostealer.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 Arch Linux AUR packages were hijacked over a weekend; the infostealer harvested browser, Electron-app and developer secrets, prompting urgent credential and token rotation for affected users.

incidents.victim: WordPress sites using Awesome Motive plugins (OptinMonster, TrustPulse, PushEngage)
incidents.vector: Malicious code was injected into the legitimate JavaScript of three Awesome Motive plugins; it waits for an admin login, creates its own admin account, and installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites were backdoored following the security incident at the major WordPress plugin developer.

incidents.victim: Global Schools Group (K-12 students, parents, staff)
incidents.vector: The FulcrumSec group exfiltrated terabytes of data from an unsecured database exposed online and leaked it after ransom negotiations failed.
incidents.impact: Passport details of children and parents, attendance records, teacher passwords and campus-visitor photos were stolen from a group managing 65 campuses across nine countries.

incidents.victim: Conti ransomware victims (1,000+ organizations worldwide)
incidents.vector: Conti affiliates hacked victim networks, encrypted data and stole files, demanding ransom to restore access and avoid public disclosure.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty to wire fraud conspiracy after extradition from Ireland; Conti hit over 1,000 victims and netted at least $150M in ransoms between 2020 and 2022.

incidents.victim: Higher-education institutions (incl. University of Nottingham, Council of Europe; Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar also listed)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters (UNC6240) exploited a critical Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, CVSS 9.8) in the Environment Management component, deployed disguised MeshCentral agents for C2, and ran a fan-out script to deface and exfiltrate data.
incidents.impact: Mandiant notified 100+ exposed organizations (68% higher education); victims including the University of Nottingham (450,000+ records) had data stolen and published on the ShinyHunters leak site. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog.

incidents.victim: Thai citizens (government healthcare-entitlements agency)
incidents.vector: Hackers allegedly stole data from a Thai government agency that manages healthcare entitlements, later posting some of it on online black markets.
incidents.impact: The personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens was allegedly exposed; the government launched an investigation.

incidents.victim: U.S. Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE)
incidents.vector: Suspected Russian hackers breached the congressman's Signal messaging account; the FBI notified him of the compromise.
incidents.impact: The Signal account of a prominent Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic was accessed, raising concerns about exposure of his communications.

incidents.victim: U.S. security-clearance holders and government/military employees
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese agents ran at least 13 fake 'consulting company' websites with AI-generated content and personas, advertising bogus jobs on hiring platforms to recruit clearance holders into sharing sensitive information for payment.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized the 13 domains used to lure current and former clearance holders, disrupting a scheme that used stolen identities, AI-generated photos and cryptocurrency to obscure foreign-government involvement.

incidents.victim: Mackay Sugar
incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted operations at Australia's second-largest sugar producer.
incidents.impact: Mackay Sugar paused cane haulage and milling at two mills in the Mackay region just as the annual sugarcane crushing season began.

incidents.victim: ServiceNow customers (primarily Australia platform release)
incidents.vector: Attackers abused an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; the flaw was reportedly exploited since at least April before being quietly patched.
incidents.impact: ServiceNow patched the platform and notified affected customers, with incidents mainly impacting its Australia release.

incidents.victim: WhatsApp users (targeted individuals)
incidents.vector: Meta says it disrupted a new NSO Group spear-phishing campaign that tried to lure WhatsApp users into clicking malicious links leading to an external site.
incidents.impact: Meta filed for contempt, alleging the campaign violated an October 2025 US court injunction barring NSO from targeting WhatsApp, and urged lawmakers to keep NSO on the sanctions list.
